statement: For TSP #44 with N up to 200K and 2s time limit, boundary-only 2-opt contributes zero score improvement. 100% random swap SA gives identical score (69.49) to 40% swap + 60% 2-opt (69.50). All SA improvement over NN construction comes from random city swaps, not segment reversals.
regime: N >= 1000, 2s time limit, grid-NN construction, SA optimization
mechanism: Random 2-opt with boundary delta cannot find improving moves in a post-NN tour because the NN construction already ensures consecutive cities are close. Random swaps work because they provide long-range diversification — exchanging two cities at distant tour positions can shorten 4 edges simultaneously.
applicability_bounds: Applies to random (non-NN-guided) 2-opt with boundary-only delta. NN-guided 2-opt with exact delta might contribute, but for N=200K the pos[] overhead makes it slower than random SA.

statement: SA swap ratio has a critical threshold near 30%: below this, SA fails to improve NN construction at all (score stays at 64.5). Above 30%, diminishing returns (40% ≈ 100% ≈ 69.5).
regime: N >= 1000, 2s time limit, SA with swap + 2-opt moves
mechanism: Random swaps provide essential long-range mixing in the SA search space. Below the threshold, the SA cannot escape the NN local basin. Above it, additional swaps find diminishing improvements because the search space is exponentially large.
applicability_bounds: Specific to random swap (uniform over all positions). Guided swaps (e.g., targeting long edges) might lower the threshold.

statement: For N=200K TSP with 2s time limit, NN-guided local search moves (2-opt, Or-opt) using a position array are slower than random moves because the O(segment) pos[] update overhead exceeds the targeting benefit.
regime: N >= 50000, 2s time limit, array-based tour representation
mechanism: For NN-guided 2-opt, after accepting a segment reversal, all positions in the reversed segment must be updated in the pos[] array. For segments of length S, this is O(S). When S is large (two geographically close cities far apart in tour), the overhead exceeds the cost of O(1) random 2-opt moves.
applicability_bounds: Might not apply with doubly-linked-list tour representation (O(1) insert/delete) or for smaller N where pos[] updates are cheaper.
